native_result.query: In which millenium did amber had the highest value and in what time interval did it peak?
native_result.HypoA: Amber has historically high and stable values in the 4th millenium BCE. with its all time peak around 3300 to 3000BCE.
native_result.HypoB: Amber had its highest value in the 4th millennium BCE (4000–3001 BCE), peaking in the interval BCE 3000–3300 (CE −3300 to −3000; calBP 4950–5250) at a Z-value of 1.54. The BCE 3000 bin (Z=1.54) is at the start of the 3rd millennium BCE; the remaining peak bins (BCE 3100/3200/3300) are in the 4th millennium BCE, which also contains the 1.46 high (BCE 3400–4000).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded data/time_series_data.csv (3601 annual rows, CE -4100..-500, all BCE; calBP=1950-CE) and data/capital.csv (39 rows, BCE 500..4300). 2) Parsed capital.csv's European decimal-comma Zamber by replacing ',' with '.'. 3) Took the raw 100-yr-bin Z-values (time_series `Amber`, capital `Zamber`) as primary and found the global maximum (1.54) and all bins attaining it (BCE 3000/3100/3200/3300). 4) Cross-checked against capital.csv Zamber (identical, max diff 0.00 over 37 overlapping bins) and against time_series `Amber_inter` (same 1.54 plateau, CE -3300..-3000), confirming interpolation does not shift the peak. 5) Mapped the peak bins to millennia using the standard convention (Nth millennium BCE = N*1000..(N-1)*1000+1 BCE): BCE 3100/3200/3300 -> 4th millennium BCE, BCE 3000 -> 3rd millennium BCE; the 4th millennium BCE also holds the 1.46 high (BCE 3400-4000), so it is the millennium of highest amber. 6) Reported the peak interval in BCE, CE(negative) and calBP.

sub_hypo.text: Amber has historically high and stable values in the 4th millennium BCE.
sub_hypo.relations: Amber Z values remain historically high and stable over this period.

sub_hypo.text: Amber reaches its all-time peak around 3300 to 3000 BCE.
sub_hypo.relations: Amber Z values reach their all-time maximum during this interval.

sub_hypo.text: Amber reaches its global maximum Z-value of 1.54 in the BCE 3000, 3100, 3200, and 3300 bins, forming a peak plateau from CE −3300 to −3000 (calBP 4950–5250).
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological amber time series covering CE −4100 to −500 and capital data covering BCE 500–4300, using raw 100-year-bin Z-values as primary measurements.
sub_hypo.relations: Amber and Zamber attain the same global maximum of 1.54 at BCE 3000/3100/3200/3300. Amber_inter preserves the same peak plateau without shifting it. Dates are related by CE = −BCE and calBP = 1950 − CE.

sub_hypo.text: The 4th millennium BCE (4000–3001 BCE) is the millennium of highest amber, containing the peak bins at BCE 3100, 3200, and 3300 and the 1.46 high at BCE 3400–4000; the equally maximal BCE 3000 bin falls at the start of the 3rd millennium BCE.
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological amber Z-values grouped into millennia using the convention that the Nth millennium BCE spans N×1000 through (N−1)×1000+1 BCE.
sub_hypo.relations: Amber Z-values equal 1.54 at BCE 3100/3200/3300 within the 4th millennium and at BCE 3000 within the 3rd millennium. Values equal 1.46 at BCE 3400–4000 within the 4th millennium.

The BCE 3000 bin (Z=1.54) is at the start of the 3rd millennium BCE; the remaining peak bins (BCE 3100/3200/3300) are in the 4th millennium BCE, which also contains the 1.46 high (BCE 3400–4000).
